§13 p5.text: Our aesthetics (§ 1), just like logic, her older sister by birth, consists of (I) a THEORETICAL first part that is instructive and general, teaching (1) about matters and potential thoughts HEURISTICALLY (chapter 1), (2) about lucid organization, METHODOLOGY (chapter 2), and (3) about the signs of what is thought and organized beautifully, SEMIOTICS (chapter 3); and (II) a PRACTICAL second part that is applied and particular.
§13 p5.alignment: The full translation preserves both branches and three subdivisions of the Latin schema; potential thoughts interprets cogitandis as possibilities rather than explicitly things to be thought, while consists of makes the structure explicit. Capitalization follows the printed English.

The independent reader personally examined the source-bound PDF rendering p43 and Latin print p5 and confirmed the complete selected sentence, punctuation, and capital letters. Potential thoughts softens the sense of what is to be thought, without material loss in context; the two parts and three subdivisions remain. The following Latin material is outside the selected place.

mexico_quotation.assessment: The independent reader assessed this one complete 67-element sentence: its theoretical schema is important, yet the full sentence is needed for comparison and is a small part of the book and translation, not a substitute for either. Under LFDA 148(I), the exact research display is conditionally justified with source, translators and author credited, unchanged text, and no impairment of normal exploitation. Future use and cumulative quotation need reassessment; CC BY-NC-ND is a distinct and conditional licence basis.
